title: Cap. X Arg. V Major: Augustine — those given to Christ are ordained to eternal life, predestined and called according to purpose, none of whom perish; given = elect; not-given = reprobate/passed over
pass_a_gloss: Unto Augustine this sentence of the aforesaid words was always pleasing: These are understood to be given unto Christ, who are ordained unto everlasting life. They themselves are those predestined, and called according to purpose, of whom none perishes, De corr. et grat. cap. 9. And in Evang. Joann. Tractat. 106. Those whom God the Son elected from the world with the Father, the same himself as man the Son received from the world from the Father. For the Father would not have given them unto the Son, unless he had elected them. You see therefore that by those given unto Christ, from Augustine's mind, nothing else is understood than the elect or predestined: And on the contrary, that by the not-given the reprobate are understood, that is, the passed over and by no means predestined, is equally confessed with the same Augustine.
pass_b_english: Augustine always liked this reading of those words: These are understood as given to Christ who are ordained to everlasting life. They are the predestined, and called according to purpose, of whom none perishes (De corr. et grat. cap. 9). And in Tract. 106 on John's Gospel: Those whom God the Son elected from the world with the Father, the same as man the Son received from the world from the Father. For the Father would not have given them to the Son unless he had elected them. So you see: by those given to Christ, on Augustine's mind, nothing else is meant than the elect or predestined. And on the contrary, by the not-given the reprobate are meant — that is, the passed over and not predestined — which Augustine equally confesses.
source_text: Augustino haec praedictorum verborum semper placuit sententia: Hi Christo intelliguntur dari, qui ordinati sunt in vitam aeternam. Ipsi sunt illi praedestinati, et secundum propositum vocati, quorum nullus perit, De corr. et grat. cap. 9. Et in Evang. Joann. Tractat. 106. Quos Deus Filius de mundo elegit cum Patre, idem ipse homo Filius de mundo accepit a Patre. Non enim Pater illos Filio dedisset, nisi elegisset. Videtis igitur per datos Christo, ex mente Augustini, nil aliud intelligi, quam electos sive praedestinatos: Et e contra, per non-datos intelligi reprobatos, hoc est, praeteritos et minime praedestinatos, apud eundem Augustinum aeque in confesso est.
